title: Forces Are Summoned from Across the Province

blocks.text: The anti-Sikh campaign quickly becomes provincial rather than local. Troops are summoned from Multan and Bahawalpur, while additional calls go out to Kasur and Attock so that pressure can be applied from several directions at once.

The hill chiefs are warned not to withhold their contingents, and fresh recruits swell the field army gathering under the Nawab's authority. With so many detachments converging, the Khalsa finds that places which once offered cover or negotiation are now being folded into a single hostile net.

Lakhpat Rai himself mounted his elephant and advanced with the force, turning the mobilization into a public spectacle of power. The result is immediate panic and dispersal, because the Singhs can see that this is no passing raid but a determined expedition meant to exhaust them.
